{{Short description|American botanist (1928–2020)}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=August 2020}}
'''Calaway Homer Dodson''' (December 17, 1928 – August 9, 2020) was an American [[botanist]], [[orchidologist]], and [[taxonomist]]. He specialized in orchids.

== Biography ==

Dodson was born in [[Selma, California]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=CZNNAQAAIAAJ&q=%22dodson,+calaway%22+1928|title=World Who's who in Science: A Biographical Dictionary of Notable Scientists from Antiquity to the Present|date=1968|publisher=Marquis-Who's Who, Incorporated.|language=en}}</ref> He specialized in orchidology very early in his career.  Over the course of his life, he made numerous expeditions to the tropics of the Americas, covering the [[Andes]] of [[Colombia]], [[Ecuador]], [[Peru]], and [[Bolivia]], where he collected specimens and discovered new species of different genera of orchids.

In 1960 Dodson began, in collaboration with [[Robert Louis Dressler|Robert Dressler]], a classification of the [[Maxillaria]] of the Americas. In 1965 he presented a study of the pollinating agents of orchids and the importance that they have on the evolutionary development of the family [[Orchidaceae]].

In the spring of 1973, Dodson was named executive director of the new [[Marie Selby Botanical Gardens]] in [[Sarasota]], [[Florida]], where he stayed for ten years,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cal Dodson, Selby Gardens' first director, dies at 91|url=https://www.heraldtribune.com/story/news/local/sarasota/2020/08/12/cal-dodson-first-director-selby-gardens-dies-91-sarasota/3353681001/|access-date=2021-04-04|website=Sarasota Herald-Tribune|language=en}}</ref> of which he was "Honorary Curator of Orchidaceae".<ref>Weber, Bruce. [https://www.nytimes.com/1990/03/25/magazine/works-in-progress-unnatural-habitat.html WORKS IN PROGRESS; Unnatural Habitat.] ''[[The New York Times]].'' March 25, 1990.</ref> In 1975, Dodson created the genus ''[[Dressleria]]'' (named after Robert Dressler) including species of the genus ''[[Catasetum]]'', from which he also reclassified other species of the genus ''[[Clowesia]]''.

After making various publications related to the world of orchids, Dodson worked on a project to compile information of the orchid family into a database, including images and facts from species from across the world.  To date, the project has collected information on 57,000 orchids.

{{botanist|Dodson|Dodson, Calaway H.}}

== Works ==
*''Clasificación de Maxillariae'' Dressler & Dodson (1960);
*''Agentes de Polinización y su Influencia sobre la Evolución de la Familia Orquidacea'' (1965);
*''Biology of the Orchids'' (1967);
*''Icones Plantarum Tropicarum'' (1998) (with 2,400 illustrations and 9 new species of [[Sobralia]] from [[Ecuador]]);
*''Illustrated Plants of the Tropics'' C.H.Dodson, John Atwood. (1980–1993);
*''Native Ecuadorian Orchids'' Volume 1, 2 y 3 (1993, 2001, y 2002).
